scope: Proposition 6.1 (Signed interior experiment) of the manuscript “Generic C1 Future Inextendibility Near Rotating Subextremal Kerr Spacetimes” (preprints/Generic-C1-Future-Inextendibility-Near-Rotating-Subextremal-Kerr-Spacetimes-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 264 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 702eacef09cb6165), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 37. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix 0 < δ < κ/32 and the prescribed finite data seminorm. Use Proposition 4.6 and Proposition 5.1 with sufficiently high fixed orders, sufficiently small losses and late support parameter, and sufficiently accurate linear residuals. For sufficiently small fixed ζ > 0 and sufficiently large T, the two entry data have smooth vacuum evolutions g± T on the strict domain (6.1), in wave-map gauge with target g. Let H± T be the relative arrays of g± T − g, and put F± T = H± T ∓ qT , Fodd T = F+ T − F− T . Then ∥F± T ∥C30 mix(ΩT ) ≤ e(κ−2α+δ)T , ∥Fodd T ∥C2 mix(ΩT ) ≤ e(κ−3α+δ)T + e(2κ−4α+δ)T . (6.2) The exact changes and all three error fields have support in v ≥ (1 − ν0)T − o(1). The time slices remain spacelike and the two moving side faces remain strict future exits. Moreover, for some c > 0, ∥H± T ∥C30 mix ≤ e−(κ/2+c)T , eo(T) ∥Fodd T ∥C2 mix + X ± ∥H± T ∥2 C2 mix ! = o(AT ). (6.3) Here every subexponential factor is at a fixed finite order. No higher seminorm of the fixed smooth background is required to be small.
